newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Finland's Ahtisaari praises S.African peace.
newsitem.headline: Finland's Ahtisaari praises S.African peace.

text.p: Finnish President Martti Ahtisaari on Tuesday praised South Africa's efforts to establish the truth about apartheid and reconcile its foes, saying other countries could follow its example.
Ahtisaari, on his first official visit to South Africa, met President Nelson Mandela at his Cape Town residence where they exchanged ceremonial awards.
Addressing a special joint sitting of parliament later, Ahtisaari said Finns admired the way South Africa had embraced the search for truth and reconciliation.

"As a country that has experienced a civil war, we know how one prefers to forget the dark sides of the past," he said. "We also know how long it takes wounds to heal in a society unless active efforts are made to promote national reconciliation."

South Africa has established a statutory Truth and Reconciliation Commission headed by Nobel laureate Archbishop Desmond Tutu to probe the human rights record of the war over apartheid, to pardon offenders and to compensate victims.

Ahtisaari, who represented the United Nations during Namibia's transition from illegal South African rule to democracy, said he was pleased to see that South Africa was playing an active and decisive role in the world body after years as an outcast under apartheid.
"We value the fact that at the U.N., South Africa has assumed a responsibility for world peace commensurate with her role," he said in a reference to Mandela's peace initative in Zaire.
Ahtisaari said the process started by the Truth Commission would probably be needed long after its term of office expired, but said the expertise should eventually be shared with the world.

"Finland will then be prepared to co-operate with South Africa in bringing forward the work and principles of the commission at the United Nations and elsewhere, if the question of internationalising the project arises," he said.
